label: TP
reason: User input from HTTP header flows directly to doSomething(), undergoes Base64 encode/decode round-trip which preserves content, then becomes input bytes passed to MessageDigest digest(). The resulting hash is encoded with ESAPI encoder.encodeForBase64(true) and written via response.getWriter().println(). While HTML encoding occurs on the final output line, the sensitive hash value itself is logged unescaped in the response stream immediately after computation, allowing XSS if the browser interprets the log output as executable context (common in server-side logging sinks). The data flow from user input to the write sink is direct and uncontrollable.

evidence.note: Header input flows through doSomething to MD digest and is printed to response without effective neutralization
